title: Texas Governor
blurb: Compare Greg Abbott and Gina Hinojosa on the issues that shape everyday life in Texas. Every stance links to sources.

issues.title: Border & immigration
issues.summary: State role in border security, migrant arrests, and cooperation with federal immigration policy.
issues.whyItMatters: Texas has spent billions on Operation Lone Star and related border measures that affect communities, budgets, and civil liberties.
issues.axisLow: Emphasize state enforcement and physical barriers
issues.axisHigh: Emphasize federal accountability and less state militarization

issues.title: Abortion
issues.summary: State abortion law, exceptions, and enforcement.
issues.whyItMatters: Texas maintains one of the nation’s most restrictive abortion frameworks after Roe was overturned.

issues.title: Public education & school choice
issues.summary: Funding for neighborhood public schools, vouchers, testing, and state oversight.
issues.whyItMatters: Texas public schools educate millions of students and are a top local employer in many counties.
issues.axisLow: Expand vouchers and state accountability pressure
issues.axisHigh: Prioritize public schools and roll back vouchers

issues.title: Property taxes & affordability
issues.summary: Homestead taxes, appraisal caps, and proposals to put money back in household budgets.
issues.whyItMatters: Housing and tax costs are among the most common pocketbook complaints for Texas homeowners and renters.
issues.axisLow: Cut school property taxes via structural reform
issues.axisHigh: Direct household relief funded from state reserves

issues.title: Health care access
issues.summary: Uninsured rates, children’s coverage, Medicaid expansion debates, and insurance rules.
issues.whyItMatters: Texas has long had among the highest uninsured rates in the U.S., including for children.
issues.axisLow: Market-focused cost cuts without Medicaid expansion
issues.axisHigh: Guarantee children’s coverage and expand access

issues.title: Energy costs & the grid
issues.summary: Electricity bills, data-center load, ERCOT reliability, and who pays for new infrastructure.
issues.whyItMatters: After Winter Storm Uri and rapid data-center growth, power bills and reliability remain front-page issues.
issues.axisLow: Open municipal monopolies to competition; industry growth first
issues.axisHigh: Freeze residential rates; make large users pay their way

issues.title: Guns & public safety
issues.summary: Firearm laws, carry rules, and approaches to violent crime.
issues.whyItMatters: Texas has expansive gun rights laws alongside ongoing debates over school and community safety.

issues.title: Voting & elections
issues.summary: Election administration, access to the ballot, and election security measures.
issues.whyItMatters: State election rules shape who can vote easily and how results are administered.

stances.summary: Supports expansive state border enforcement through Operation Lone Star, including barriers, state arrests, and cooperation with federal deportation efforts.

Criticizes Abbott-era border spending priorities and argues for practical border policy with stronger federal accountability rather than indefinite state militarization; campaign focus is affordability and schools more than border theater.
Has signed and defended Texas abortion restrictions after Roe fell; endorsed by anti-abortion groups including Susan B. Anthony List.
Supports restoring abortion protections in Texas and removing criminal penalties tied to the current ban framework.

Championed private-school vouchers (Legislature dedicated about $1 billion for two years) and pushes classroom screen limits, tougher teacher-misconduct penalties, and directing 70% of school funding to classroom instruction.
Opposes vouchers as diverting public money; pledges to replace Education Commissioner Mike Morath, pause STAAR-based A–F accountability, and restore funding focus to neighborhood public schools.

Proposes eliminating school district property taxes for homeowners via constitutional amendment, lowering the homestead appraisal cap to 3%, and requiring two-thirds voter approval for local tax increases.
Proposes a one-time $1,500 household payment drawn from excess Rainy Day Fund balances, plus property-tax relief tied to adequately funding schools so districts are not forced to raise local rates.
Focuses on lowering premiums and out-of-pocket costs through an Essential Benefits plan and capped co-pays for some medications, without campaigning on Medicaid expansion.
Centers on guaranteeing quality health care for every Texas child, supports Medicaid expansion as a means, and backs bans on bad-faith insurance denials.

Supports retail competition against municipal utility monopolies to lower bills; more recently paused new data-center grid connections pending audit and backs requiring data centers to fund their own infrastructure.
Would direct the PUC to freeze residential rates until large users like data centers pay their own infrastructure costs; criticizes Uri-era gas company windfalls and consumer bill impacts.

Campaign messaging emphasizes public safety through tougher bail and prosecution while Texas under his tenure has maintained expansive gun-carry laws; protecting gun rights is a stated Republican priority.

Has supported stronger firearm safety measures as a Democratic state lawmaker; campaign public materials emphasize schools and affordability more than a detailed new gun platform—position summarized from legislative record context.
Has signed and defended Republican-backed election security legislation during his tenure; continues to frame election integrity as a governing priority.

As a Democratic legislator and nominee, supports broader ballot access and opposes measures Democrats describe as voter suppression; detailed governor-specific voting plank is thinner than education/affordability.

quiz.prompt: Texas should dial back state-led border militarization and push the federal government to take clearer responsibility.
Texas should restore broader legal access to abortion.
Texas should reverse private-school vouchers and prioritize funding neighborhood public schools.
The state should send direct household relief (for example Rainy Day refunds) rather than focusing mainly on eliminating school property taxes.
Texas should guarantee quality health coverage for every child, including via Medicaid expansion if needed.
Residential electric rates should be protected—including freezes—until big users like data centers pay for their own grid costs.
Texas should adopt stronger firearm safety rules than it has today.
Texas election rules should prioritize easier ballot access over additional security restrictions.
